summary:
RiverGuard is an AI-powered river erosion monitoring and geospatial intelligence platform developed by Team AethronXDIU from Daffodil International University. The project addresses Bangladesh’s growing riverbank erosion challenges by transforming satellite observations into accessible, actionable insights. Leveraging NASA satellite imagery, particularly Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), alongside weather and river-discharge data from Open-Meteo, RiverGuard provides interactive geospatial visualization, historical imagery comparison, and environmental context to help identify changing river patterns, erosion-prone areas, and char formation.

Aligned with NASA Space Apps Challenge’s “Dancing with the SARs” challenge, the platform demonstrates how Earth observation and radar remote-sensing data can support river landscape monitoring. RiverGuard aims to empower local communities, researchers, and decision-makers with better awareness of environmental changes, helping improve disaster preparedness, risk awareness, and informed decision-making to protect vulnerable communities, agricultural land, and infrastructure.
details:
RiverGuard: AI-Powered River Erosion Monitoring and Intelligence Platform

RiverGuard is an AI-powered river erosion monitoring and geospatial intelligence platform developed by Team AethronXDIU from Daffodil International University. It focuses on addressing riverbank erosion in Bangladesh, where changing river courses threaten communities, agricultural lands, infrastructure, and livelihoods.

How It Works:
RiverGuard integrates NASA GIBS satellite imagery with weather and river-discharge data from Open-Meteo to create an interactive river monitoring platform. Users can explore selected river regions through interactive maps, visualize satellite imagery, compare historical observations, and understand changes in river morphology and char formation. The platform combines Earth observation data and geospatial visualization to make complex environmental information easier to interpret and identify potentially vulnerable areas.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
RiverGuard aims to improve public awareness of riverbank erosion, support community preparedness, and provide useful environmental insights for researchers and decision-makers. Its intended impact is to help protect vulnerable communities, agricultural land, infrastructure, and livelihoods by making satellite-based information more accessible and understandable.

Tools and Technologies:

  • NASA GIBS – Satellite imagery and Earth observation data.
  • Open-Meteo API – Weather and environmental information.
  • Web development technologies – Platform development and data integration.
  • Geospatial visualization – Interactive mapping and historical imagery comparison.

Creativity and Innovation:
The innovative aspect of RiverGuard is bringing satellite imagery, environmental data, and interactive geospatial visualization together in a single platform. Instead of requiring users to interpret complex satellite datasets, it presents geographical and environmental changes through accessible visual insights.

Team Considerations:
Our team considered Bangladesh's geographical vulnerability, satellite data availability, data reliability, user accessibility, platform usability, and future scalability. We focused on creating a solution that could be useful not only for technical experts but also for local communities and organizations working on disaster preparedness and environmental protection. Our long-term vision is to strengthen community resilience through accessible Earth observation and river monitoring intelligence.
